fixes.explanation: Right, friend. She kissed His feet and then anointed them with the perfume (Luke 7:38). Feet, not head. The text has her standing behind Him at His feet.

The head is a fair guess, friend, but the text puts the perfume on His feet. She kissed His feet and anointed them with the perfume (Luke 7:38). Her tears and her hair are already at His feet in that same verse.

Handing the jar to Simon would be a very different story, friend. The text says she anointed His feet with the perfume (Luke 7:38). Nothing in that verse has her handing it to anyone. Simon is busy in his own head, which we're about to hear about.

The text says the Pharisee did say this to himself. He thinks, “If this man were a prophet, He would know who this is and what kind of woman is touching Him…” (Luke 7:39). Keep that in mind for the next verse.

That's not what Jesus says. He tells Simon, “You did not greet Me with a kiss, but she has not stopped kissing My feet since I arrived.” (Luke 7:45). Simon gets no kiss in that line. The kissing Jesus describes comes from the woman.

False is right. Jesus says, “You did not greet Me with a kiss, but she has not stopped kissing My feet since I arrived.” (Luke 7:45). Simon did not greet Him with a kiss. The woman has not stopped kissing His feet.
Head is the first blank. Jesus says, “You did not anoint My head with oil…” (Luke 7:46). That's what Simon didn't do. Well done, friend.
Feet fills the second blank. Jesus says “…but she has anointed My feet with perfume.” (Luke 7:46). Head for Simon's missing oil, feet for her perfume.

No beard in this verse, friend. Jesus names the head for the oil Simon didn't give and the feet for the perfume the woman did (Luke 7:46). Beard never comes up. Check the two body parts He actually names.
The text says the opposite. Luke 8:1 says, “The Twelve were with Him…” as He traveled from one town and village to another. So the apostles are along for the trip.
That's it. The text says, “These women were ministering to them out of their own means.” (Luke 8:3). Joanna, Susanna and many others were helping with what they had.
Sending word ahead isn't what the text says about these women. It says, “These women were ministering to them out of their own means.” (Luke 8:3). Nothing in that verse mentions sending word ahead.

Teaching the crowds isn't what the text says about these women. Luke 8:1 has Jesus preaching and proclaiming the good news. About the women it says, “These women were ministering to them out of their own means.” (Luke 8:3).
